data.name: Kayani
data.gender_notes: Kayani is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Persian word 'kayan' meaning 'advisor' or 'leader'. In Islamic history, the Kayani dynasty ruled parts of the Indian subcontinent and were known for their wisdom and just rule. The name Kayani carries the meaning “Advisor, Leader” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Kayani usually hope their child will grow to embody advisor, leader and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for a child who will grow up to be a wise and just leader.
data.etymology: Kayani belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Advisor, Leader.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kayani total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_arabic.name: كيانى
in_arabic.meaning: اسم مشتق من كيان و معناه القوة و الرفعة

in_urdu.name: کیانی
in_urdu.long_meaning: کیانی ایک ایسا نام ہے جو قوت، رفعت اور ثبات کو ظاہر کرتا ہے۔ یہ نام بعض اوقات مضبوط اور ثابت شخصیت کے حامل افراد کے لیے استعمال کیا جاتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: कियानी

in_pashto.name: کیاني
in_pashto.long_meaning: کیاني یو داسې نوم دی چی د قوت، لوړتیا او ثبات څرګندونه کوي. دا نوم ځینې وختونه د قوي او ثابت شخصیت لرونکو کسانو لپاره کارول کیږي.

By embodying the qualities of a wise advisor and knowledgeable teacher, a Kayani serves as a beacon of guidance, helping others navigate the spiritual terrain and deepen their connection with the Divine.

historical_references.reference:
General Muhammad Ayub Khan appointed General Muhammad Moazzam Khan Kayani as the Commander of the Pakistan Army on 15 November 1972, following the Bangladesh Liberation War.
Reference: The Dawn Newspaper, Pakistan.
historical_references.context: Appointment as Commander of the Pakistan Army after the Bangladesh Liberation War

historical_references.reference:
General Pervez Musharraf appointed General Jehangir Karamat as the Chief of the Army Staff on 5 November 1998, and later removed him and appointed General Pervez Musharraf himself as the COAS on 12 October 1999. General Karamat was later given the honorary title of 'Chief of the Army Staff (Retired) Kayani'.
Reference: The News International, Pakistan.
historical_references.context: Appointment and removal as Chief of the Army Staff, given the honorary title 'Retired Kayani'
